To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Wnt5 induces ROR1-ROR2 heteroolimerization to enhance leukemia cell proliferation and migration.
Wnt5 signaling induces the oligomerization of ROR1 with ROR2, which recruits guanine exchange factors to activate Rac1 and RHOA, thereby promoting the migration and proliferation of leukemia cells.
Wnt5A induces ROR1-ROR2 heterooligerization to enhance leukemia cell chemotaxis and cell proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new mechanism by which ROR1/R2 heterooligomeric complexes regulate the chemotactic and proliferative properties of CLL cells.
the molecular mechanisms by which Wnt5a enhances leukemia cell chemotaxis and growth and how these effects can be therapeutically targeted.
the molecular mechanism of ROR1/R2 heterooligomeric signaling and the role of Wnt5a in leukemia chemotaxis, migration, and engrafment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Wnt5 induces ROR1/2 heterooligomeration to enhance leukemia chemosensitivity, chemotaxis, and proliferation.
Wnt5A-induced ROR1/R2 oligomerization is required for WNT5A signaling that promotes leukemia proliferation and migration, and this interaction is inhibited by UC-961.

ROR1/R2 heterodimerization is essential for Wnt5A signaling in CLL and that this signaling is critical for CLL proliferation and migration and that this signaling can be blocked by the anti-ROR1 monoclonal antibody, cirmtuzumb (UC-961) which is currently in a phase I/II clinical trial.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Wnt5A induces heterooligomerisation of ROR1 and 2 to enhance leukemia cell proliferation, chemotaxis and metastasis.
Wnt5/ROR1 signaling is required for the chemotaxis and engrafting of leukemia cells in vivo.
Wnt5-ROR1/2 interaction induces Rac1/RhoA activation and CLL chemotaxis and growth, and this process is inhibited by UC-961.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ROR1 and Wnt5a are critical mediators of chemotaxis and survival of leukemia cells and that targeting ROR1 with a monoclonal antibody may provide an effective therapy for patients with leukemia.
Wnt5/ROR1 signaling is a key regulator of CLL migration and proliferation.
the ROR1/R2 receptor complex is a key player in Wnt5a–mediated noncanonical signaling in CLL and other malignancies.
